 Mary Walrath-Holdridge USA TODAY Oct. 26, 2026, 5:35 p.m. ET Hear this story Nearly 1,000 pounds of beef jerky snacks sold in seven states have been recalled, according to a notice from the Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS).
 The 946 pounds of ready-to-eat beef jerky products were packaged and sold using unauthorized USDA labels and were not actually properly inspected by the agency. As a result, the jerky may not meet U.S. food safety standards and therefore be unsafe to eat, the FSIS said.
 Imperio Distribution LLC initiated the recall on Oct. 24 after standard FSIS surveillance uncovered the false labels. So far, there are no confirmed reports of illness or injury related to the jerky.
 FSIS inspects certain imported meat, poultry and egg products after they arrive in the United States, even if they were previously inspected in their country of origin. The agency does this to ensure imported products meet the same food safety, labeling and regulatory requirements that apply to domestically produced goods.
 Food imported without undergoing that process is often recalled because it may contain undeclared allergens, harmful bacteria or other contaminants that put consumer health and safety at risk.

 Which products are recalled?
 All the recalled beef jerky came in 2-ounce sealed bags. The top of the package is "carne seca" in Spanish next to the English term "beef jerky."
 It was packaged between January and October 2026. All bear "1885" inside the USDA mark of inspection.
 Imperio Fuego Beef Jerky
 Imperio Original Beef Jerky
 Imperio Limón Beef Jerky
 Where was recalled jerky sold?
 These items were distributed to various retail locations in seven states, according to FSIS, including:
 Illinois
 Indiana
 Iowa
 Michigan
 Minnesota
 Missouri
 Wisconsin

 Customers with the recalled products should not consume them and should throw them away or return them to the place of purchase, according to FSIS. Anyone concerned about an illness or injury related to the product should contact their health care provider.
 Consumers with questions about the recall can contact Imperio Distribution at 630-532-9560 or manuelcortes33@gmail.com.
